newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Savage Resources gains from demand for germanium.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Savage Resources gains from demand for germanium.

text.p: Savage Resources Ltd said on Thursday germanium produced as a by-product at its Tennessee zinc refinery continues to make a big impact on the bottom line.

David Rice, president of Savage Zinc Inc, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Sydney-based Savage Resources, said germanium producers were benefitting from robust demand in a range of applications that have kep prices above US$1,000 a kg in 1996.
Savage produces about 20 tonnes of the metal each year against world output of between 80 and 100 tonnes, Rice said.
Germanium was fetching over US$1,000 a kg a price which has enabled Savage to sell some metal forward, Rice said.
In 1995/96 ended June 30, Savage's germanium sales amounted to more than A$20 million, up from A$10.2 million the previous year, company figures show.

The fibre optics industry remains a major consumer of germanium, although more exotic applications such as in the making of solar cell windows used on spacecraft were helping push up demand, Rice said.
Belgian's Union Miniere SA, the former owner of the zinc refinery, is the sole buyer of the metal from Savage, Rice said.
Substitutes for germanium include zinc sulphide and antimony trioxide.
The refinery supplies about eight percent of U.S. zinc demand.
However, Savages's managing director, Jim Wall, welcomed the revenue that diversification provided.
"If you stick with one commodity, it can be a pretty tough time between lunches," Wall said.
Earlier this year, germanium producers urged the U.S. Defense Logistics Agency to speed up the sale of stockpiled metal as rocketing prices threatened substitution and loss of market.
